title: Let Engram's Git read admit repositories with pinned submodules, in step with TermAl's submodule capture, so Questly and Phoenix checks can count
outcome: Engram's live Git read at evaluate and done treats a repository with initialized, pinned and Git-clean submodules as current at the check's root commit, by the same rules TermAl's capture uses, so a correct check in Questly or PhoenixCodeNav is not refused just because the repository has submodules.
acceptance: On real Questly commits on Linux and Windows, and on real PhoenixCodeNav commits on Windows, in a disposable clean checkout with every submodule initialized at its pin, an ordinary launcher run records committed input; evaluate and done accept that check with evaluations on, and done accepts it on bound work with evaluations off.
A dirty child, a child off its pin, an uninitialized child and a dirty root are each refused at evaluate and done, naming the cause, on Linux and on Windows
Engram and TermAl, which have no submodules, behave as before, and the existing evaluation matrix rows still pass
There is no exception list; Git-ignored output such as PhoenixCodeNav's .codenav is outside the verdict; no historical evaluation, verification or seal changes
Both items (this and TermAl's w-c07c410dac75) close together, only on executed host rows from point 1 on Linux and Windows, run against the exact commits being landed

completion.summary: Admit clean initialized pinned and nested submodules through ordinary recursive Git status at evaluate and done; preserve named refusals, ignored-output behavior and existing records. Landed, pushed and installed exact fd candidate.
